items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: You see, Paul Gaten put this on the black market.

ctx.x: I think True is certainly a standard. I mean, not just...

Well, it isn't a standard, Dick. It has never been put on the market as a number. It could have gotten to be a big thing when Paul Gaten put it on. Yeah. But, so the company wouldn't pay us off, the writers. You see, Paul Gaten put this on the black market. He said he had written a song in the Scotchrell and I. And, uh, Linden, New Jersey is where the record company was. They lined up the records to not pay us.
Well, you know, to me, that's a standard because people still play it today.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: Now Paul Gayton is the one that changed the name from You Don't Love Me to True.

ctx.x: Yeah. Fine. He said to tell you that he thinks that Cottrell and a couple other guys, a trio recorded a tune that you and Cottrell wrote. And one of the names was True.

Do you remember that? Do you have another name? That was the theme song. The actual title of the song is You Don't Love Me. Now Paul Gayton is the one that changed the name from You Don't Love Me to True.
